summary: Low-income adults who won a lottery for Medicaid coverage saw fewer unpaid medical bills sent to collections and less depression, though not more work.
realLife: Oregon drew names by lottery for a Medicaid program, so researchers could compare winners and non-winners. Winners reported almost no catastrophic medical spending and were far less likely to borrow or skip other bills over medical expenses. Credit reports showed a quarter fewer unpaid medical bills sent to collections. Winners used more care, felt less depressed, and did not change their employment or earnings.
sources: https://www.nber.org/programs-projects/projects-and-centers/oregon-health-insurance-experiment/oregon-health-insurance-experiment-results (NBER summary of the Oregon Health Insurance Experiment results)
